title: Starter Launch Visual System: modular sticker sheets, motion tokens, and in-page CTA microcopy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a compact, reusable visual system for the Quickstart landing that focuses on: 1) modular "sticker" assets (small, composable icons/frames used across hero and step cards), 2) short motion tokens (micro-animations for attention and transitions), and 3) a small set of in-page CTA microcopy variations for A/B testing. Goal is to reduce visual debt, make screenshots predictable across feature flags, and give Engineering a lightweight animation API to implement without heavy runtime cost.
acceptance_criteria: Sticker sheet exported as SVG sprites + 1x/2x PNGs for each icon and frame
Three motion token specs with Lottie + CSS fallback (hover, entry, success) and max 350ms duration
Responsive screenshot guidelines: full-width desktop (1440px), tablet (1024px), mobile (375px) with automated capture instructions
CTA microcopy set (3 variants) documented with expected conversion signal and placement rules
Figma file with component library, token documentation, and implementation notes shared with engineering
Performance budget: animations must not increase hero bundle by more than 30KB gzipped
tasks: Audit existing hero and step screenshots to identify 12 high-variance elements
Design sticker sheet: 24 atomic elements across 3 scales
Define 3 motion tokens and deliver Lottie + CSS examples
Create screenshot capture runbook and Playwright spec for automated captures
Draft CTA microcopy variants and annotate A/B targets for PM
Handoff meeting with ENG for implementation constraints and accessibility review
Create export pipeline: Figma -> optimized SVGs -> spritesheet generator -> CI artifact storage
design_decisions: Prefer small, single-purpose illustrations (sticker approach) instead of full-bleed hero illustrations to keep screenshots consistent between releases
Use Lottie for motion tokens for fidelity on web and mobile; provide CSS keyframe fallbacks for lowest cost path
Max animation length set to 350ms to balance discoverability and accessibility (reduced motion considerations included)
Visual language to favor monochrome strokes with a single accent color to match Redwood brand and reduce color variance in screenshots
Screenshots will avoid transient state (tooltips, toasts) — annotate where ephemeral overlays are acceptable

implementation_notes: Provide sprite SVG + JSON index for runtime mapping (name -> path)
Lottie usage: import JSON via CDN with low-priority fetch; show compressed animated SVG placeholder until loaded
CSS fallback: keyframe sequences for entry/hover/success using transform + opacity
Animation hooks: data-motion-token="entry-01" attributes to allow engine to bind without extra JS
assets_needed: SVG sticker sheet (24 elements) — mono stroke + accent color
PNG exports at 1x and 2x for legacy clients
Implementation spec document for ENG with perf budget
screenshot_plan: Baseline captures: current landing hero (no animation) for comparison
Variant A: sticker mosaic, left-aligned headline
Variant B: compact tile stack with motion token entry
Variant C: enterprise-trust CTA with short trust line
Capture pipeline: Playwright script in repo -> triggers on branch -> stores artifacts in /artifacts/onboarding/visuals/<branch>
accessibility_considerations: All motion tokens must respect user 'prefers-reduced-motion'. Sticker icon stroke widths must meet AA contrast when used on background tints. CTAs must have >4.5:1 contrast against their backgrounds. Export checklist includes an accessibility pass and color contrast screenshots.
handoff_plan: Schedule 60-minute synchronous handoff with ENG + PM (invite sent for 2025-03-05)
Create GH issue ENG-6142 with implementation checklist and link to assets
Add Playwright capture job to infra pipeline and run nightly against staging to validate screenshot stability
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Animations increase page bundle or main-thread CPU — Mitigation: lazy-load Lottie and provide CSS fallback; enforce 30KB gzipped budget
Risk: Screenshot variability across devices — Mitigation: standardize baseline data, use Playwright to capture deterministic viewport and mock network
Risk: Design drift across releases — Mitigation: publish token docs and require design review for any new sticker additions
